title: The rain timing contrast was above zero in one of four British moth samples in 1992-2015
abstract: We tested whether moth community change had a stronger rain link in the catch month than in the following month. We used 516 pairs of trap-months in England and Scotland in two periods from 1992 to 2015. A joint model controlled temperature differences, sampling effort, sample dates, trap by month and linear time. The outcome used a finite-catch correction. The catch-month minus following-month rain slopes were +4.64, -2.50, +7.37 and -5.06 turnover units per 100 mm larger absolute rain difference between adjacent years. Only early Scotland had a four-test interval above zero, from +1.84 to +12.91. Its interval included zero with other catch thresholds and after removal of some source years. These data do not show a common rain timing response. Few sites and years, selected catches, country weather and rain-dependent capture limit inference. The future-month comparison is an imperfect timing diagnostic. This exploratory follow-up uses the same biological records as prior campaign studies. It does not identify a causal climate effect or test air pollution. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, numerical checks and a figure are included. External record-level data stay outside the publication and can be rebuilt from pinned sources.

display.caption: Catch-month rain slopes and catch-month minus following-month rain slope contrasts. Bars show approximate intervals with a four-test correction within each target. Only early Scotland has a primary interval above zero. The result depends on catch thresholds and source-year selection.
